messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P0 security pager — abnormal token reuse pattern detected
incident-bot: source: auth-service / token-indexer, regions: prod-us-east-1, prod-eu-west-1, metrics: 401 spike + token reuse signature, runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/security/token-reuse
Mia (oncall): I’m on it. grabbing the latest auth logs for the period 2026-03-15T09:10Z -> 09:20Z
Mia (oncall): Raj — can you join for triage? this looks like cross-region replay
Raj (secops): joining. pinging sec tooling, starting correlation on token hash 0x7fa3b2
Lucas (sre): I’m here — any customer-facing degradation?
Alex (support): customer metrics dashboard shows ~6 customers with elevated 401s since 09:08, two have reported errors via support channel. I flagged them in the ticket.
Chao (engineer): seeing suspicious S3 PUT activity from a non-standard agent near the same timeframe. path looks external: s3://uploads-external-76/logs/prod-auth/2026-03-15/09/*. Could be exfil of debug logs?
Raj (secops): if external S3 is involved we should assume leaked tokens or key material in logs. Mia — can you run a quick grep for "Authorization: Bearer" and "svc-" in those log files?
Mia (oncall): running now, will paste results. output snippet:
```
2026-03-15T09:11:02Z auth: INFO token=svc-sync-9af3 user=svc-sync src_ip=54.23.122.11 action=login
2026-03-15T09:11:05Z auth: DEBUG headers={... Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci...} request=/v1/internal/sync
```
Mia (oncall): confirmed. svc-sync token appears in logs and matched by external S3 put time.
Raj (secops): immediate containment recommended: 1) block IP 54.23.122.11 at edge; 2) revoke svc-sync token(s); 3) disable external log forwarder consumer; 4) rotate service tokens and issue emergency creds.
Lucas (sre): I can push the firewall block rule now. Applying block to edge WAF and cloud firewall for 54.23.122.11. (done)
DevDeployBot: deploy started: disable-extern-log-forwarder v2026-03-15T09:25Z by Lucas (sre)
DevDeployBot: deploy succeeded in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 in ~45s
Mia (oncall): Raj — can you run revocation command for svc tokens? sample: `authctl revoke --service svc-sync --reason "suspected-leak-2026-03-15"`
Raj (secops): executing now. output:
```
$ authctl revoke --service svc-sync --reason "suspected-leak-2026-03-15"
Revoked: svc-sync-9af3
Revoked: svc-sync-bridge-02
```
Raj (secops): all known svc-sync tokens revoked. starting rotation procedure with KMS owners.
Chao (engineer): I’ll queue a hotfix to remove any PII/debug dumps from the auth service logs and push sanitize branch. patch in code review now.
Alex (support): drafting initial customer comms: "We detected abnormal activity affecting authentication for some customers; mitigation in progress. We’ll provide more details in 2 hours." Want review from legal/security before send.
Raj (secops): legal looped in. Also recommending to rotate any downstream API keys that could have been present in the same logs (list will be compiled).
Mia (oncall): I see session replay attempts from a different IP range too (185.93.45.0/24) — might be multiple actors. Lucas, can you throttle token issuance rates and add stricter rate limits on auth endpoints?
Lucas (sre): enabling stricter throttles for /v1/internal/* and /v1/token/exchange. Changes applied as temporary quota (5r/s per client) in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Monitoring.
Raj (secops): scanning for other service tokens in the suspected S3 bucket. Also initiating list of potentially impacted customers — cross-referencing access logs.
Mia (oncall): quick impact numbers from logs so far: ~12 distinct service tokens observed in leaked files, 6 customers with user-visible 401 spikes, no evidence yet of account takeovers.
Chao (engineer): running grep across historical logs to verify whether any private keys or KMS plaintext were present — preliminary: no KMS plaintext seen, but two stack traces include `env.SERVICE_KEY` — likely debug leak.
Raj (secops): escalate to infra team to rotate any long-lived keys referenced. Mia please compile inventory of keys referenced in logs and post here.
Mia (oncall): will post in 15m. working with Chao on automated script to list key identifiers.
DevDeployBot: incident ticket INC-2026-0315-77 created and linked: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-0315-77
Alex (support): opened support tickets for the 6 customers and applied temporary workaround guidance for integrations.
Raj (secops): recommended timeline (immediate): block IPs, revoke & rotate leaked tokens, disable external forwarder, sanitize logs. next (within 2h): customer notifications, rotate downstream keys, CI secret scan.
Chao (engineer): approved hotfix merged to prod-branch; sanitization pipeline running to overwrite leaked debug fields in logs that were forwarded externally.
Lucas (sre): monitoring shows auth error rate trending down after throttles and token revokes. still watching for replays.
Mia (oncall): handing off to Raj for secops lead. I’ll be available for follow-ups. Raj, take the on-call baton. :white_check_mark:
Raj (secops): taking over. team, please add any actions you take to INC-2026-0315-77 and label with `security/containment` or `security/rotation`. I’ll coordinate customer comms with Alex and legal.
Alex (support): drafting customer advisory and will post to status.redwood.ai once legal signs off. timeline aimed: 2 hours.
Raj (secops): next steps: full key inventory, revocation/rotation, confirm no PII exfil, postmortem owner assigned (Raj). If evidence of data exfil beyond logs, escalate to executive comms.
Mia (oncall): noting handoff in calendar. thanks all. :pray:
